clue.text: In speech nails a few words

indicators.note: in speech tells the solver to go by how a word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: nails on fingers or paws are claws

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that, in conversation, nails are worth a brief mention.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical unit is a short group of words containing a verb, so a few words fits.

clue.text: Dog beginning to munch a foreign dish

parts.note: the chow is a Chinese dog breed

indicators.note: beginning to means just the opening letter of munch

parts.note: ein is German for a

explanation.surface: A dog starting to eat a dish of foreign food.
explanation.definitionFit: This stir-fried noodle meal is a Chinese dish.

clue.text: Cornered in a seaside borough, soldiers needing to escape

indicators.note: needing to escape means the soldiers go out of the borough word

parts.note: Torbay is a seaside borough in Devon, England
OR, other ranks, are soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops trapped in a coastal town, desperate to get out.
explanation.walkthrough: Torbay, in Devon, covers the resort towns of Torquay, Paignton and Brixham.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal held at bay is cornered by its pursuers, unable to escape.

clue.text: Second drink? It may make you see spots

definitions.text: It may make you see spots

parts.note: a tipple is a drink

explanation.surface: A second drink might leave you seeing spots before your eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See spots' suggests drunkenness, but stippling is a painting technique of dots.
explanation.definitionFit: Stippling is painting or engraving in small dots, so it produces visible spots.

clue.text: Mark made by caveman, made but half obliterated

parts.note: Stig of the Dump is the caveman of Clive King's children's novel

indicators.note: half obliterated means only the first half of the word made survives

explanation.surface: A mark scratched on a cave wall by a caveman, now half worn away.
explanation.walkthrough: Stig is the caveman hero of the British children's book 'Stig of the Dump'. 'half obliterated' keeps MA from the second 'made'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace or a visible blemish, a figurative or literal mark.

clue.text: Person briefly in the office gets man captivated

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
Ted is a man's name

explanation.surface: A temporary office worker gets a man smitten.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tempted has been lured or enticed, drawn in as if captivated.

clue.text: Sponsor wanting party on the up, what you'd expect in civilised chap

indicators.note: in places the reversed party and the expected value within the chap word

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman

indicators.note: on the up in a down clue means the party word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a do is a party
par is the normal or expected standard

explanation.surface: A sponsor without a party, acting as you'd expect of a gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A godparent sponsors a child at baptism, vouching for their religious upbringing.

clue.text: Across Hatred and rage Left conjured up for monarch

indicators.note: conjured up suggests the letters are magicked into a new form

explanation.surface: Hatred and fury on the political Left raised a king from the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth-century king of Wessex who beat the Danes is the only English monarch so styled.

clue.text: Hope maybe to acquire expensive stuff, making uncertain movement?

parts.note: Bob Hope the comedian, so Hope is an example of someone called Bob
bling is slang for flashy expensive jewellery

explanation.surface: Bob Hope's ambition to get rich, pictured as faltering, wobbling progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hope maybe' is a definition by example: the comedian Bob Hope.
explanation.definitionFit: To bobble is to move with a jerky, wobbling motion, as a ball does on rough ground.

clue.text: A record is kept by French author who may explore a particular line

definitions.text: who may explore a particular line

indicators.note: kept by means the group goes inside the author's name

parts.note: Jean Genet was a French novelist and playwright
a log is a record

explanation.surface: A French writer keeps a record of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line' means a family line of descent, not a line of text.
explanation.definitionFit: One who traces family descent investigates a particular bloodline.

clue.text: Someone in field having party — there's slight resentment about that

indicators.note: about tells us the resentment word goes round the party word

parts.note: a miff is a petty fit of pique
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A farmhand throws a party and feels a little resentment about it.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, mid-off is a fielding position near the bowler on the off side, and also the fielder standing there.
explanation.definitionFit: Mid-off names a cricket fielder, a player stationed in the field.

clue.text: This writer making comeback — this writer's getting award

indicators.note: making a comeback signals the word for the writer turned backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
the setter's own is my

explanation.surface: An author returns after a break and wins a prize for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emmy is the American television industry's annual award.

clue.text: Joke act, duet being funny, given marks

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words

indicators.note: funny in the sense of odd, so the letters of act and duet are put out of order

explanation.surface: A comic double act tells jokes and gets scored by judges.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing that has been punctuated has been given commas, stops and other marks.

clue.text: Trifle recipe for getting lad fed?

parts.note: fiddle with (rearrange) the letters of faddle and they give lad fed, so the answer is a recipe for producing those words

explanation.surface: A trifle pudding recipe for feeding a hungry boy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: 'fiddle' is the signal to mix up 'faddle', which yields LAD FED. 'Trifle' looks like the pudding; it is the verb meaning to mess about.
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle-faddle is to fuss over trivia, which is what trifling means.

clue.text: National guards would be organised by Louis and me?

definitions.text: National guards would be organised by Louis and me?

indicators.note: organised means the letters of national guards are rearranged, here into the answer plus Louis

explanation.surface: The musketeer boasts that he and King Louis would organise the guards.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove LOUIS from NATIONAL GUARDS and rearrange the rest. Dumas's hero, a musketeer, served King Louis XIII, and the clue is his voice.
explanation.definitionFit: D'Artagnan, the Gascon musketeer, served in the King's guards under Louis XIII.

clue.text: Scavenger's beginning to make off with waste material

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of the scavenger word

parts.note: to pillage is to plunder, making off with goods

explanation.surface: A scavenger starts carrying away rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Spillage is material that has been spilt and wasted.

clue.text: Unstable type, artist taking drug, one with nothing, is given therapy inside

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual artist

indicators.note: inside places the following group within the drug word

parts.note: dope is slang for a drug
I is the Roman numeral one
O looks like zero, nothing
OT is occupational therapy

explanation.surface: A volatile character, an artist on drugs, alone with nothing, gets put into therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: A radioactive form of an element is an isotope that decays: an unstable type of atom.

clue.text: Darling daughter, serious but heartless

parts.note: D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: heartless removes the central letter of the word for serious

parts.note: earnest means serious

explanation.surface: A beloved daughter who is solemn but unfeeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are terms of endearment for a loved one.

clue.text: Northern city characters turning up to eat a northern fish

indicators.note: to eat means the city's letters go round the following pair
turning up in a down clue reads the city's letters upwards

parts.note: the letters of Leeds, a city in northern England

explanation.surface: The people of a northern city start eating a fish from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: The sand eel is a small slender sea fish, food for puffins.

clue.text: Remove certain content from paper containing bad English

indicators.note: containing means the newspaper's letters hold the next two pieces

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper
ill means bad

explanation.surface: Cutting some content from a newspaper that is full of poor English.
explanation.definitionFit: To fillet a fish or joint is to take the bones out, removing part of what is inside.

clue.text: What could get one avoiding a subject ultimately?

definitions.text: What could get one avoiding a subject ultimately?

indicators.note: the letters before us, rearranged, could get the answer, so this phrase is the anagram signal
ultimately picks the final letter of subject

explanation.surface: Asking what leads someone to dodge a topic in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Mixing AVOIDING A plus T, the last letter of 'subject', gives the answer, and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Divagation is wandering off a topic, a digression that steers away from the subject.

clue.text: River and lake subside

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A river and lake whose water levels drop.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a Cornish river reaching the sea at Falmouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Waters that subside drop in level, so they fall.

clue.text: Skill rendering sort of musical passage

definitions.meaning: a strong point, something one excels at
a passage to be played loudly

explanation.surface: A talent for performing a certain kind of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A forte is one's strong suit, and also a section of music played loudly.

clue.text: Good weapon — it has a metallic lustre

parts.note: a lance is a knight's weapon

explanation.surface: A fine weapon whose polished metal shines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glance' is a mineralogists' term for any ore with a shiny metallic lustre, such as lead glance (galena).
explanation.definitionFit: In mineralogy the word names a lustrous ore, a sulphide with a metallic sheen.

clue.text: See 7
Teacher shortly gathering chaps not initially held in music class

indicators.note: gathering means the teacher word takes the chaps word in
shortly cuts the last letter from the teacher word

parts.note: a tutor is a teacher

indicators.note: not initially removes the first letter of the word for chaps

parts.note: men are chaps

explanation.surface: A tutor brings a group of men together for a music lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical direction means a note is sustained for its full value, held.

clue.text: Swear as member drowning in beer

indicators.note: drowning in puts the limb word inside the drink word

parts.note: ale is beer
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: Claiming under oath that a body part was drowned in beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert or declare, as one would swear to a claim.
